The vector xi+Z has the law of sqrt(C) times a standard vector, and Z is used only for the inequality. Cov Y(f_i),Y(f_j)<=C I follows from the variance bound on real combinations of orthonormal f_j. The block inequality on j=N+1..M, with W(f_j) standard, gives the Cauchy property from (1). Letting M tend to infinity gives both lines of (3), the second by taking N=0. checks.claim: C2: Literal raw h_R matrix identity, projection Y(P_N h), complexification, basis independence, linearity, and stability of the error at arbitrary relative rates.
checks.reason: Identity (9) is exactly operator-note (13) with g_j=W(f_j), together with long-interval additivity. Hence sum_j<=N Y(f_j)<h,f_j>_H=Y(P_N h), which converges to Y(h) in L2 by the extended variance bound, and operator-path convergence gives (4). No filter is commuted through the mask or a wave group. Linearity holds for jointly Gaussian noises because the finite sums are linear and pass to Lp limits. Stability uses the tail bound (10), uniform in n, plus the finite part bounded by sqrt(s_N(n))||M_N|| through (8), with covariance at most trace times I. This split needs no rate relation and works for nets. M_Dn=M_R-M_Yn follows from linearity. No nonlinear wave ordering is used.

checks.claim: C3: H_Gamma null quotient and (2pi)^d spectral form, Schwartz inclusion, heat C_epsilon properties, real structure, and separable G.
checks.reason: With h(y)=int f(x)g(x-y)dx, form (11) matches foundation Section 4 including (2pi)^d. Evenness of mu makes it real on real tests. Schwartz functions enter through expanding cutoffs, since the correlation converges in Schwartz topology against tempered Gamma. In the unitary convention, hat(p_epsilon*f)=exp(-epsilon|xi|^2/2) hat f. Therefore C_epsilon and I-C_epsilon are positive selfadjoint contractions, and C_epsilon tends strongly to I by domination and density. Heat preserves Schwartz functions, so it acts on the completion. No physical mask multiplier is asserted on the quotient, consistent with foundation Proposition 3. G is separable because the fiber is separable and the base is sigma-finite.

minor: Section 4 proves the Phi isometry on tensors and extends by density. Section 5 then uses the pointwise formula (12) on general smooth compact F without stating that it equals the extension. This is a one-line routine omission and is disclosed rather than silently accepted. Fixed-support uniform tensor approximants make the right side of (12) converge pointwise in H_Gamma while Phi F_n converges in G, so the two agree almost everywhere. The Bochner computation needs nothing further.

The Section 5 Bochner integral needs strong measurability of (t,x)->v in G, which follows from (5) and (17) with b=0. That estimate is displayed later in Section 6. The dependence is not circular, only an order of presentation.
Section 6 patches versions on overlaps of rectangles. This should be read with a nested exhaustion so that overlaps have dense points. Optional wording only.

The cutoff family depends on the chosen auxiliary J off Phi H, so Theorem 2 is an existence statement for a retaining coupling rather than a canonical function of W. The note does not claim otherwise and does disclaim minimal-span measurability. Downstream use should not treat the family as W-determined.
The letter P is used for three objects: P_N, the range projection P, and P_delta. The Theorem 1 uniform D_n bound is also implied by the Y_n bound. Both points are cosmetic.
